reviews.comment: Took over Summer session. Class material was imported from last Summer.  This a go as fast as you want but not slow semester. Print lecture slide notes, take notes, and use open notes for quizzes each week. He did offer a few "pop-up" things to do for extra credit. I had all 10 week assignments completed in 5 weeks, less the two group assignments.

awesome professors one of the best TAMU has to offer. Have him for two classes neither are workload heavy! and his exams are very easy not much studying pay attention in class and you will be fine, he cares more about you taking in info rather than testing you over it, he does emphasize the things you need to know for exams gives extra credit

This class is almost an exact copy of SPMT 230. He has his TA grade everything, so it's pretty easy to get an A. Just follow all his instructions and you'll do fine. He sends out random weird emails that have nothing to do with the class, but he's a really nice guy. This is my third or fourth class with Guinn and I would honestly take him again.

Dr. Guinn posted youtube links for this class's lectures at the beginning of the semester, and we have not received much feedback or interaction since. This course is all online, mostly consisted of busywork in the form of discussion posts, papers, and short tests, and was quite unorganized. He may be better in-person, but avoid his online classes.

(Over 3 courses) Dr. Guinn is my all-time favorite professor in the Sport Management Major. If you have the opportunity to take one of his courses, you will love them. His lectures are engaging and class is a great time. His exams are based on his lectures/slides. If you pay attention and take decent notes, you can easily make an A in his courses.

I have taken one course with this professor before and there are assignments and lecture material directly copied over from the previous class. His webpage is awfully organized and he does not communicate with the class hardly at all. I honestly do not know what he's done all semester since posting all the lecture videos and slides back in January.
